  "reasoning": "All 20 fields agree with their own captured Math Academy worked solutions. Transposition exchanges row and column counts, giving 5×3 and 2×2. Reading the vector diagrams in grid units gives a=(4,0), b=(-2,2), c=(-4,6) for q-20435, hence λ=1/2; a=(6,0), b=(0,4), c=(6,8) for q-120244, hence λ=2; a=(0,-3), b=(-1,2), c=(3,3) for q-120260, hence λ=-3; and j=(-2,-4), k=(4,0), l=(-6,4) for q-120279, hence λ=-1 and μ=-2. A linear ODE is homogeneous when its forcing term is identically zero; the forcing terms are respectively 0, x, -4x and x, 0, -5x. Associated homogeneous equations replace the forcing term with zero. For q-130991, option 1 is also equivalent after division by x on intervals excluding zero, but option 3 exactly preserves the original differential operator and matches the source. Initial conditions specify y and y′ at the same point: I only in q-339256 and I and III in q-339251. The first system in q-339256 is still formally an initial value problem, although its data are inconsistent with the equation at x=0: -y′(0)+2y(0)=3, whereas cos(0)=1, so it has no classical solution satisfying those data. The requested classification does not assert existence. Deleting the indicated row and column gives minors -33, -7, and 36pq. Finally, the minor 9t-8 equals t²+12 precisely when (t-4)(t-5)=0.",
